threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Rust DOCX comparison, revision, inspection, editing and rendering engine, exposed through a native CLI, PyO3 Python library/CLI, wasm-bindgen browser/Node APIs, a Node CLI and an optional Python MCP stdio server (README.md:12-16; src/lib.rs:15-35; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381). Normal processing consumes document bytes and produces document bytes or views; it does not automate Word or LibreOffice (src/lib.rs:7-11). Filesystem authority differs materially: the native CLI publishes caller-selected ambient paths through staged publication; Python and Node CLI helpers use ordinary ambient file writes; the MCP adapter holds a root directory capability for input reads and output publication; WASM byte APIs do not expose native publication (src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:153-225; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:106-111; src/lib.rs:163-165). Explicit self-update and release workflows independently exercise network, executable-replacement, signing and publication authority.
assets: Confidential source DOCX, legacy DOC and Markdown content; revision authors, comments, metadata, media, generated agent views, reports, patches, clean documents and redlines (src/lib.rs:15-30; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:185-217). MCP edit exports have distinct derived destinations under the selected root and out_dir: clean.docx, redline.docx, patch.diff, report.json, optionally redline.pdf and redline-page-NN.png.

Integrity of edit targets and their source revision. EditPlan.source_sha256 is optional, and when supplied the actual source hash must match or STALE_SOURCE is returned; author labels are document data rather than authenticated identities (src/edit.rs:97-108,2081-2092).

Host filesystem content reachable with the invoking OS account; MCP's selected root directory capability; CLI Markdown resource roots; ambient native renderer font directories; output staging and existing output bytes (src/publication.rs:153-199,203-225,421-505; src/bin/jubarte.rs:2858-2871,2937-2943; src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652).

Availability of the embedding Python process, native process or browser/Node WASM instance. Ordinary admission defaults allow 64 MiB compressed/per-part, 256 MiB inflated total, 10,000 entries and XML depth 256; comparison defaults instead allow 512 MiB compressed/per-part and 2 GiB inflated total (src/admission.rs:63-100).

Installed jubarte executable integrity and the authority to replace it. Current trusted release-key configuration is empty, so the updater uses release checksums rather than mandatory signatures (src/update.rs:44-48,198-210,245-257).

Release signing secret reference ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, GitHub release publication token reference GITHUB_TOKEN, local PyPI token reference UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN and local npm/Cargo publishing credentials. These are separate capabilities and are not document-processing credentials (.github/workflows/release.yml:230-275,278-307,356-369; scripts/release.sh:919,934-954,1069).

GitHub review comments/checks and external Jules session capability. Ordinary reviewer and companion-remediation workflows receive different permissions and apply different caller gates (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-52,259-272,320-324).
trustBoundaries: Untrusted package bytes cross into ZIP/OPC/XML parsing and rendering. Admission prechecks budgets, checks duplicate entries and shared ZIP structural defects, and bounds actual inflated reads rather than trusting declared sizes (src/admission.rs:439-470,531-535). The shared checked ZIP opener rejects defects; debug is an intentional unchecked diagnostic exception (src/opc/archive.rs:15-19,34-51). Checked XML APIs and raw permissive DOM APIs are separate caller contracts, explicitly distinguished by SECURITY.md:51-65.

Untrusted legacy DOC is a separate OLE/FIB/piece-table parsing path, subsequently converted into Markdown/DOCX; it is not covered merely by identifying DOCX ZIP admission (src/legacy_doc.rs:13-50). Embedded fonts, image decoders and layout are additional native parser surfaces identified by Cargo.toml:107-110.

Native CLI operators select ambient input/output paths. src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273 invokes publication::publish_paths, whose root=None backend opens output parents with ambient authority (src/publication.rs:203-225,431-446). Outputs stage beside their destination in .jubarte-<UUID>.partial/bytes, with Unix staging directory mode 0700 and exclusive creation (src/publication.rs:472-505). Publication stages all files first but commits per file; failures can leave named committed outputs, and Windows directory synchronization is intentionally a no-op (src/publication.rs:100-130,168-174,387-405). This is not an all-files transaction.

Python and Node CLI callers retain ambient local filesystem authority. Python's _read_side consumes caller paths and _write calls Path.write_bytes; Node's read and write helpers call fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:73-83,126-133; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-56,106-111). Native staged-publication properties cannot be assumed for these helpers.

The MCP operator grants a directory root once; a connected stdio client can invoke all registered read/write tools within that grant. --root defaults to current working directory, is expanded/resolved, and must be a directory; no HTTP listener or application authentication is configured in this entrypoint (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381). Python containment checks are early diagnostics; actual reads and publications use _native._OutputRoot, backed by cap_std directory authority and portable relative-write validation (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:69-108; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:153-199,228-273,431-463). overwrite is a per-call replacement capability, defaulting false. ToolAnnotations are metadata, not a separate authorization layer (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,153-160).

CLI Markdown image targets cross into local filesystem reads only through a selected resource root: explicit --resource-path wins, otherwise the Markdown file's parent, otherwise '.' (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2937-2943). The loader canonicalizes and holds that directory capability, applies image policy and reads relative to the capability; URLs are not fetched by this loader (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2877). This capability is separate from output publication authority.

Native renderer font discovery is ambient OS-account access, independent of MCP's document/output root. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides per-user locations; absent it, Windows uses APPDATA/jubarte/fonts, macOS HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, and other native platforms XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts (src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652). Native discovery also examines named system/Word font directories and HOME/Library/Group Containers/UBF8T346G9.Office/FontCache/4/CloudFonts/<family>; the document-supplied family must be a single normal path component for that derived cloud directory (src/convert/font.rs:2225-2236,2281-2309).

Browser/Node WASM callers pass byte arrays and JSON options into the engine. The bindings disable default engine features, omit native publication on wasm32 and support comparison-budget overrides; the binding explicitly warns that its 2 GiB inflated default can exceed practical WASM heap capacity (jubarte-wasm/Cargo.toml:18-23; src/lib.rs:163-165; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:63-97). Hosting applications own admission tuning, upload authorization, origin policy, worker isolation and persistence.

Explicit jubarte self-update crosses from GitHub release metadata/assets into executable replacement. Repo is jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines; the chosen archive member is jubarte-<version>-<platform>/jubarte[.exe]; SHA256SUMS.txt is configured; extracted binary must lstat as a regular file (src/update.rs:25-27,91-109,198-210,299-321). Without --check/--yes, noninteractive runs stop before lookup; installation requires confirmation unless --yes; explicitly selected versions may downgrade (src/update.rs:120-125,144-160,234-247). Current RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean signature enforcement is inactive (src/update.rs:44-48,274-285).

Tag-driven GitHub release automation builds platform archives/wheels with read-only job permissions, then a separate contents:write job signs when configured, computes checksums and publishes dist/* to the triggering tag's release (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,51-89,230-275,295-321,356-369). The signing secret is scoped to the signing step, decoded into RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.<random>/keyN and removed by an EXIT trap; the signing tool and runner are recipients of this authority (.github/workflows/release.yml:261-307).

The local release script separately publishes the Rust package, both npm packages and PyPI artifacts. Typed version confirmation precedes pushing unless YES is set, then each registry operation uses its own tool/account authority (scripts/release.sh:877-919,929-959,1063-1069). The script calls a downstream app checkout, but that application's implementation is absent from this repository and is not included as inspected architecture (scripts/release.sh:141-175).

PR automation crosses repository-controlled PR source, descriptions and tool output into external actions and agent sessions. The normal review workflow excludes fork/Dependabot PRs and grants contents:read, pull-requests:write and checks:write; companion remediation additionally gates session creation on TRUSTED_USERS=['arthrod'] and selected events, uses AUTO_CREATE_PR and require_plan_approval=false (.github/workflows/jules-review.yml:19-50; .github/workflows/jules-el-conejo-review.yml:35-52,259-272,320-324). External action internals, Jules integration permissions and runtime restrictions are not present here.

CI/docs workflows execute checked-out repository code on self-hosted runners for pull_request events. Workflow token permissions are contents:read and checkout disables persisted credentials, but host filesystem, network, persistent-state isolation and runner admission controls are external deployment controls (.github/workflows/ci.yml:13-40,72-99; .github/workflows/docs.yml:42-86,98-99).

Validated audit refinements: package admission's extension-based selection does not cover relationship-resolved notes with non-XML suffixes (src/admission.rs:533-570; src/document_comparer.rs:6318-6328,6461-6479). Admission also ignores DTD while the raw DOM disagrees on declaration boundaries (src/admission.rs:798-820; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:539-547,660-662). These are findings, not assertions that the intended policy is fully enforced.
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier can control document bytes, ZIP/XML structure, relationships, embedded media/fonts, Markdown content and document metadata that callers choose to process. This does not grant control of trusted environment variables, arbitrary operator-selected paths, release credentials or executable installation decisions.

A connected MCP client can choose tool arguments, source files and output destinations inside the operator-granted root and request overwrite=true. These are existing tool capabilities; new security impact would require exceeding the root grant, unintended disclosure to another actor, bypassing promised replacement restrictions or attacking the host process.

A library/WASM caller can choose API input bytes and exposed options, including input-limit overrides. A hosted service may expose a narrower subset, but no such service deployment or tenant model is established by this repository.

A PR contributor can control PR source/text subject to repository contribution permissions and workflow event gates. Same-repository authorship, trusted-user session gates, self-hosted runner admission and external agent authority must be evaluated separately; fork authors are not automatically authorized for secret-bearing Jules workflows.

Release-asset modification or privileged tag/release control is a distinct prerequisite for updater supply-chain impact. Ordinary document control does not confer it; checksums fetched with release assets do not independently authenticate the publisher (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80).
securityObjectives: Reject malformed/unsupported packages and enforce active resource limits before expensive parsing; do not interpret archive member names as arbitrary extraction paths or execute document macros. Checked ZIP admission and XML policy are component controls, while process CPU/memory isolation remains a host obligation (src/admission.rs:13-28,439-470,531-535; SECURITY.md:69-74).

Preserve MCP document read/output confinement through held directory capabilities despite path changes, and reject unsafe output paths and output symlinks rather than relying solely on Python resolve checks (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:75-108; src/publication.rs:153-199,228-273,431-463).

Preserve existing output bytes through staging failures; report partial commits and durability uncertainty accurately. Do not claim atomic publication across multiple files or native publication parity for Python/Node write helpers (src/publication.rs:100-130,168-174,387-405).

Keep Markdown image reads inside the selected resource root and avoid automatic network fetches from image targets (src/bin/jubarte.rs:2851-2877,2937-2943). Keep this control distinct from native font discovery and output confinement.

Reject stale edit snapshots when source_sha256 is supplied, and preserve the documented caller obligation when it is omitted (src/edit.rs:103-106,2081-2089). Revision author fields and SHA-1/FNV comparison keys must not become authentication claims (SECURITY.md:76-85).

Install only the explicitly selected supported-platform release artifact after applicable checksum, signature-policy and regular-file checks, with the documented interaction/downgrade policy (src/update.rs:91-125,144-160,198-257,307-321).

Keep release signing, GitHub release writes, registry publishing, PR comments/checks and external remediation sessions as independent capabilities with their own event/account gates and external permission prerequisites.

When docprops scrubbing is requested, remove identifying properties by authoritative OPC metadata target before returning outgoing package bytes; conventional-path-only sanitation misses relocated parts (src/scrub.rs:357-384; src/opc/mod.rs:655-667).
assumptions: Source observation is the current authorized working checkout; architecture reviewer reported HEAD 6a34e1c498bcf403ed98a443ac11a9fced70892f from a read-only current-state query. The parent artifact directory contains a different hash, but directory naming is not authority for another revision. No history or alternate revision was inspected.

No user deployment context, supplied threat model, source inventory or knowledge base was provided. No public service, HTTP exposure, tenant isolation, process sandbox or production hosting configuration is established.

SECURITY.md is repository policy data, not evidence that every implementation guarantee has been exhaustively verified. Its latest-release support, untrusted-input policy and process-limit requirement apply as stated; this pass did not run tests or application code.

Signing documentation describes both signature-capable future releases and the checksum-only current phase. Actual constants remain RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None; therefore signature support must not be described as current mandatory verification (docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-80; src/update.rs:44-48,245-249,274-285). This is an explicit staged configuration rather than a newly established vulnerability.

Documentation/configuration disagreement: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24 says GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN are used when set. src/update.rs:198-211 configures neither auth_token nor auth_token_from_env. Offline architecture review of the locked cached self_update 1.3.1 dependency showed CommonBuilderConfig defaults auth_token=None and auth_token_from_env=false, with environment lookup opt-in. Preserve both the documentation claim and effective anonymous configuration; impact here is authentication/rate-budget behavior, not evidence of token disclosure. Dependency evidence: cached self_update-1.3.1/src/backends/common.rs:1027-1053 and backends/github.rs:391-406; repository version anchor Cargo.lock:2552-2553.

The broad library statement that entry points admit input (src/lib.rs:30) has documented exceptions: debug intentionally opens unchecked ZIPs and raw parse_xdocument is not an input-policy API (src/opc/archive.rs:15-19; SECURITY.md:54-65). Treat these as distinct interfaces rather than projecting ordinary admission guarantees onto all public helpers.

MCP root, explicit Markdown resource root, environment-selected font root, output paths and installed binary path are runtime/operator choices absent from supplied deployment context. The configuration chains and derived child names are established; exact machine-specific absolute values are not.

Native font lookup uses ambient directories even when the hosting MCP adapter confines document and output paths. MCP root confinement is not a whole-process filesystem sandbox (src/convert/font.rs:2228-2234,2281-2309,2637-2652).

WASM/native bindings reuse the engine but have materially different host capabilities and budgets. Browser resource isolation and remote-service limits are external caller obligations; the WASM binding explicitly warns about default comparison memory limits (jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:80-85).

The external Jules actions, hosted service permissions, self-hosted runner lifecycle/network/filesystem controls and downstream jubarte-app implementation were not available as inspected repository source. Workflow configuration establishes grants and gates but does not prove external enforcement.
This independent architecture review is not completed security-audit coverage and contains no validated vulnerability findings.

Focused parser worker returned source-backed candidates but failed before its final full-coverage result. Parent independently validated retained candidates. Its files are not counted as fully audited without a completed review. Inventory and fully reviewed file reconciliation remains explicitly partial.

findings.title: Listing revisions in a renamed notes part bypasses XML depth admission
findings.summary: A DOCX with an internal footnotes or endnotes relationship targeting `notes.bin` passes the filename-based XML policy gate. Listing revisions, or comparing documents through the notes pipeline, then parses that part recursively without checking its depth. A small deeply nested part can exhaust the native stack or trap the WASM instance.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can trigger the public byte APIs with a small package and no privileged configuration. The established consequence is loss of the embedding process or WASM operation, not code execution. Process isolation recommended by SECURITY.md limits collateral impact.
severity.changeConditions: A service that processes uploads in a shared unsandboxed process increases impact; mandatory checked parsing of every relationship-selected XML part eliminates this path.

confidence.rationale: Parent source review confirms both the suffix-only admission decision and the unchecked relationship-to-parser path; no runtime exploit was executed.

codeEvidence.label: revisions input
codeEvidence.explanation: `get_revisions` accepts caller-controlled package bytes and invokes admission before reading the main part.

codeEvidence.label: xml admission
codeEvidence.explanation: Admission decides whether to validate XML solely from the filename suffix; an auxiliary notes.bin is only drained and counted.

codeEvidence.label: xml main only
codeEvidence.explanation: The extra check for nonstandard XML filenames covers the main document only.

codeEvidence.label: notes resolve
codeEvidence.explanation: Footnotes/endnotes are selected from internal relationship targets, independently of their filename extensions.

codeEvidence.label: notes parse
codeEvidence.explanation: The selected notes bytes reach the unchecked recursive DOM parser without an intervening XML policy check.

codeEvidence.label: xml recursion
codeEvidence.explanation: The raw parser recursively handles each nested element without an active depth limit.

codeEvidence.label: compare notes
codeEvidence.explanation: The comparison pipeline independently parses the same relationship-selected notes using the unchecked parser.

codeEvidence.label: checked parse
codeEvidence.explanation: The existing checked API demonstrates the missing boundary: it validates the actual string before constructing a DOM.

rootCause.summary: The violated invariant is that every XML string sent to the recursive DOM parser must first satisfy the active XML policy. `admit` only checks `.xml`/`.rels` entries and specially handles the main part; `notes_part_names` follows valid OPC relationships to any filename, and both revision listing and comparison send those auxiliary bytes directly to `parse_xdocument`.

findings.remediation: Validate every relationship-selected XML string with the active InputLimits before DOM construction, including footnote/endnote parts irrespective of filename; propagate refusal from both revision listing and comparison.

assertions: The package can keep its normal main XML shallow while a related notes.bin contains deep XML.
Byte-size caps do not enforce element depth.
counterEvidence: Main parts with unusual extensions receive a special XML check.
inspect::parse_part_within validates actual XML strings and is not included as vulnerable.
Raw parse_xdocument is intentionally unchecked; this finding is its admitted-package caller bypass, not that public contract alone.
limitations: Exact crash threshold depends on platform and stack size; no runtime reproduction or deployment assertion.
validation.summary: Verified public `get_revisions` input admission, internal relationship resolution without suffix restrictions, bounded ZIP loading that does not validate auxiliary XML, and the recursive parser sink. The comparison notes pipeline has the same missing check.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes → admit suffix gate → PartFs → notes_part_names relationship target → unchecked notes DOM parse → recursive parse_element.

impact.why: Availability of the hosting process or WASM instance.

likelihood.why: Direct public document-input boundary with no optional feature required.

reachability.summary: The attacker controls document bytes processed by the public library/bindings; no network service exposure is assumed. Host availability is affected when the consumer processes the supplied document.
reachability.outcome: Stack exhaustion/process termination or WASM trap

attackPath.summary: Supply an otherwise valid DOCX whose footnotes/endnotes relationship targets a small deeply nested XML part with a non-XML suffix, then have a consumer list revisions or compare it.

remediationTests: Integration cases for nonstandard footnote/endnote extensions at and beyond a small explicit XML-depth limit.
Cover both get_revisions and compare with the same relationship-selected deep part.

findings.title: Converting an HTML altChunk can allocate billions of table columns
findings.summary: A small DOCX containing an HTML altChunk with a huge numeric `colspan` can exhaust memory or CPU during conversion. The importer accepts the value as `usize` and generates one `<w:gridCol>` per column before any layout or raster limit applies.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can trigger excessive allocation through the public conversion API with a small input and no configuration changes. Availability of the host process or WASM instance is affected; no remote service deployment, code execution or data theft is established. External process limits constrain collateral impact.
severity.changeConditions: A shared upload-processing process increases impact; bounded table columns and a checked expansion budget remove the amplification.

confidence.rationale: Parent source review confirms direct numeric parsing, table-close dispatch, unbounded output loop, and public conversion reachability; no application execution.

taxonomy.category: Unbounded allocation from HTML numeric input

codeEvidence.label: conversion public
codeEvidence.explanation: Caller-provided DOCX bytes enter public PDF conversion and reach with_pages/with_layout.

codeEvidence.label: conversion layout
codeEvidence.explanation: Admission happens before HTML expansion; the referenced chunk bytes are sent to altchunk::expand and resulting XML goes straight to a DOM.

codeEvidence.label: chunk repeat
codeEvidence.explanation: Each altChunk reference is loaded, decoded to HTML and converted by html_to_wml.

codeEvidence.label: html parser
codeEvidence.explanation: The HTML tokenizer dispatches each td/th opening tag to Builder::start and table closes to end_table.

codeEvidence.label: span input
codeEvidence.explanation: The colspan string is parsed into an unrestricted usize and retained on the cell stack.

codeEvidence.label: span count
codeEvidence.explanation: end_table sums cell spans into the table's column count without a cap.

codeEvidence.label: span output
codeEvidence.explanation: The column count controls one allocated XML grid-column string per iteration.

rootCause.summary: `Builder::start` treats `colspan` as any positive usize. `end_cell` retains that span, and `end_table` sums it into `cols` before a `0..cols` loop materializes XML for every column. Package admission runs on the original DOCX and does not bound this derived HTML table size.

findings.remediation: Enforce a practical maximum cell span and checked per-row/total column counts before generating any table markup; charge all generated WML to an expansion budget and return a typed input-limit refusal.

counterEvidence: ZIP and XML budgets limit original package entries; they do not limit the numeric colspan or derived WML.
Page raster MAX_PAGE_PIXELS is reached later and does not constrain this importer.
limitations: No runtime reproduction or exact memory measurement; numeric allocation consequence follows directly from the loop.
validation.summary: Verified that even one cell in one small HTML chunk reaches the unrestricted span parser and that closing the table generates a grid sized by the span. A billion-column positive value fits both 32-bit and 64-bit usize and implies tens of gigabytes of grid markup without needing integer overflow.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes → with_layout admission → altChunk relationship load → HTML td colspan → cell span → end_table cols → per-column String growth.

likelihood.why: A small numeric HTML field directly determines work.

reachability.summary: Untrusted document suppliers reach this importer whenever the public renderer processes their DOCX. The input need not be large, and no release/OS authority is needed.
reachability.outcome: Memory/CPU exhaustion and process termination or WASM failure

attackPath.summary: Provide a small internal HTML altChunk with a single table cell using an oversized colspan, then convert the containing DOCX to PDF/PNG or request its layout.

remediationTests: Unit tests with a small configured column cap cover the inclusive limit, one above it, oversized numeric values, and sums of several otherwise valid spans.
Integration test through a DOCX altChunk confirms refusal occurs before grid generation.

originalEvidence.sink: src/convert/altchunk.rs:461-485 sums spans and appends one w:gridCol per column

findings.title: Repeated HTML chunk references bypass conversion memory budgets
findings.summary: A DOCX can repeatedly reference one modest HTML part. The renderer admits the small original package, then copies and converts that chunk separately for every reference and concatenates all generated XML. The resulting allocation and work can exceed package budgets by orders of magnitude.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier can choose many tiny references and one ordinary HTML part that fit original byte/depth/entry limits. The direct outcome is memory/CPU exhaustion in the embedding process or WASM instance. No service deployment is assumed; process isolation limits collateral impact.
severity.changeConditions: Shared unsandboxed upload processing increases impact; a cumulative expanded-byte/node budget enforced before append removes this path.

confidence.rationale: Parent inspected admission order, relationship load, raw HTML acceptance, per-reference conversion and unlimited output append; no runtime reproduction.

codeEvidence.label: conversion public
codeEvidence.explanation: The public renderer receives caller-controlled DOCX bytes and enters the shared layout path.

codeEvidence.label: conversion layout
codeEvidence.explanation: Only the original package is admitted; relationship-selected HTML is expanded afterward and the resulting string is parsed directly.

codeEvidence.label: chunk repeat
codeEvidence.explanation: Each repeated altChunk is independently loaded and converted, and its entire WML result is appended to a growing output string without cumulative accounting.

codeEvidence.label: chunk html
codeEvidence.explanation: A normal raw HTML chunk is accepted directly, so the multiplier needs neither MIME encoding nor a malformed colspan.

rootCause.summary: `with_layout` admits only the original ZIP. `altchunk::expand` treats each reference independently, reloads the same bytes, rebuilds its HTML as WML and appends the result to one String, without a reference/output budget. The package's original bytes and entries therefore do not bound its expanded representation.

findings.remediation: Pass an active cumulative expansion budget into altchunk import, enforce checked limits before each conversion/append and before DOM construction, and refuse inputs exceeding expanded bytes/nodes. Caching repeated conversion can reduce CPU but must not replace the total-output limit.

counterEvidence: External URLs are not fetched; attack uses an existing internal part.
Original ZIP budget, XML depth and entry limits remain effective on stored input but not the derived repeated string.
This path needs no oversized table span and survives a per-span fix.
limitations: No dynamic reproduction or memory measurement; exact failure depends on platform and external resource limits.
validation.summary: Verified a standard self-closing `w:altChunk r:id` form is repeatedly matched, the same existing internal relationship may be used each time, and normal HTML paragraphs can supply the repeated body. For example, thousands of small references to a roughly megabyte HTML body imply gigabytes of expanded XML although the package stores that body once.

dataflow.summary: Admitted original DOCX → repeated same-rId altChunk lookup → repeated HTML-to-WML conversion → out.push_str per reference → oversized DOM/layout.

likelihood.why: No optional configuration, large source input, or invalid HTML required.

reachability.summary: Document suppliers control both reference multiplicity and internal HTML content through the ordinary public renderer boundary.
reachability.outcome: Memory or CPU exhaustion of the embedding process/instance

attackPath.summary: Supply an otherwise readable DOCX with many altChunk references to the same small HTML part, then invoke conversion or shared layout.

findings.title: Loading an admitted document can recurse into markup hidden inside its DTD
findings.summary: A conventionally named DOCX main XML part can put deeply nested literal markup inside a quoted DTD entity value. Admission treats the entire DTD as one ignored event, while the downstream raw DOM parser stops skipping at its first `>` and interprets the remaining embedded tags recursively. This bypasses configured XML depth limits and can terminate the native host or trap WASM.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document supplier controls ordinary main-part bytes, and the public admitted-document API reaches the recursive parser without privileged options. The supported impact is process/instance availability loss, constrained by recommended external process isolation; no XXE, file access or code execution is claimed.
severity.changeConditions: Mandatory DTD rejection during admission or checked parsing before DOM construction removes this path; a shared unsandboxed document service would increase impact.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified both repository parser implementations and cached locked quick-xml 0.42.0 DTD scanner behavior. No application code or crafted input was executed.

taxonomy.category: XML grammar differential bypassing recursion policy

codeEvidence.explanation: main_document later reads admitted main-part bytes and passes them to the raw DOM parser.

codeEvidence.label: dtd raw
codeEvidence.explanation: The raw parser skips declarations only to their first greater-than character, even inside a quoted internal entity value.

codeEvidence.label: xml recursion
codeEvidence.explanation: Nested markup left within that value is then consumed by the recursive element parser.

codeEvidence.label: xml dtd reject
codeEvidence.explanation: The checked API already rejects DTD entirely, but package admission does not share this control.

rootCause.summary: Admission and the consuming DOM disagree on declaration boundaries. `check_xml_depth` ignores quick-xml's complete DocType event, so nesting within the quoted internal subset is invisible to its depth accounting. `parse_document` skips only through the first `>`, then `parse_element` interprets remaining embedded tags and recurses without a depth guard.

findings.remediation: Reject DocType events in package admission consistently with validate_xml_with_limits; also make raw declaration skipping grammar-correct or defensively bound recursion so parser differentials cannot bypass policy.

assertions: The main part can retain a shallow real w:document after the internal subset.
A single entity containing several nested tags suffices; the early two-entity illustration is not a required precondition.
counterEvidence: validate_xml_with_limits rejects DTD; callers using it are not included.
This is not external entity resolution or entity expansion.
Archive byte limits still apply, but stack-exhausting nesting fits well below them.
limitations: Exact stack failure depth is platform-specific; no runtime reproduction or remote deployment is asserted.
validation.method: independent parent static source and locked-dependency trace
validation.summary: Verified current quick-xml 0.42.0 parser/dtd.rs:28-30,124-135,194-199 preserves quoted entity values while scanning the internal subset, and reader/state.rs:163-173 emits the entire declaration as DocType. Admission ignores that event. The raw parser uses its first-'>' search regardless of quotation and resumes element parsing, so sufficiently deep literal tags can exceed the admitted depth.

dataflow.summary: DOCX main XML → quick-xml DocType → ignored admission event → stored bytes → raw first-'>' declaration skip → recursive embedded tag parsing.

likelihood.why: Source-established public parser path with attacker-controlled main XML.

reachability.summary: The public byte-oriented WmlDocument API is a sufficient boundary; the document supplier requires no environment control or raised input budgets.
reachability.outcome: Native stack exhaustion or WASM trap

attackPath.summary: Have a consumer admit DOCX bytes and access WmlDocument::main_document with a main-part DTD containing deeply nested literal XML inside a quoted entity value.

findings.title: Malformed WMF text records amplify small images into large retained strings
findings.summary: Converting a DOCX with a crafted embedded placeable WMF can allocate hundreds of megabytes from a roughly 200 KB media part. WMF text counts may read across their declared record boundaries, while the parser advances by the much smaller declared record size and retains each overlapping decoded string.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can reach this path through public rendering with ordinary admitted package sizes. The supported impact is memory/CPU exhaustion in the native host or WASM instance; no out-of-bounds native memory read or code execution is claimed. The 384-pixel canvas cap and external process limits constrain collateral effects but do not limit retained text.
severity.changeConditions: A shared unsandboxed renderer increases impact; record-local field/count validation plus a cumulative text/record budget removes this amplification.

confidence.rationale: Parent source trace confirms image relationship loading, WMF dispatch, full-file count checks, retained owned strings and declared-size advancement. Allocation arithmetic is source-derived, not a runtime measurement.

taxonomy.category: Malformed record length permits overlapping allocation amplification

codeEvidence.label: conversion public
codeEvidence.explanation: The public PDF renderer accepts document bytes and reaches shared layout.

codeEvidence.label: conversion layout
codeEvidence.explanation: ZIP admission occurs before renderer media interpretation; it bounds stored bytes, not allocations derived from malformed WMF records.

codeEvidence.label: media input
codeEvidence.explanation: A document-controlled embedded image relationship is resolved and passed to decode_image.

codeEvidence.label: media resolve
codeEvidence.explanation: The internal media bytes are copied from the resolved package part without transformation of record counts.

codeEvidence.label: wmf entry
codeEvidence.explanation: decode_image tries the metafile interpreter first and retains all returned MetaText values.

codeEvidence.label: wmf record
codeEvidence.explanation: The WMF loop only checks each declared record length against the entire file; field readers still use the full file slice.

codeEvidence.label: wmf text
codeEvidence.explanation: EXTTEXTOUT/TEXTOUT use attacker-declared character counts against the entire data, allowing reads into subsequent records.

codeEvidence.label: wmf owned
codeEvidence.explanation: Each accepted text slice is decoded into a newly owned String and retained as MetaText.

codeEvidence.label: wmf advance
codeEvidence.explanation: The next iteration advances by declared record size rather than consumed text extent, enabling overlapping text copies.

rootCause.summary: `raster_wmf` validates `size * 2` against file bytes remaining, but never constrains field reads to that record. `META_EXTTEXTOUT` and `META_TEXTOUT` independently use their count fields to slice the entire metafile, then `wmf_text` allocates a String. The main loop retains that value and advances only by declared record length, so many tiny malformed records repeatedly copy overlapping file suffixes.

findings.remediation: Parse each WMF record through a slice limited to its declared extent and validate every fixed field, optional rectangle, text count/padding and coordinate array against it before allocating; add a cumulative decoded-text/record budget.

counterEvidence: Whole-buffer slice checks prevent Rust memory unsafety; this is parser resource amplification.
WMF object count is clamped and canvas MAX_SIDE is 384, but neither controls the texts vector.
Valid record-local counts would consume input proportionally and would not produce this overlap.
limitations: No runtime reproduction; exact heap growth/failure depends on String allocation and host limits.
Geometry siblings also use full-file readers; only the text-allocation consequences are independently validated here.
validation.summary: Verified that text counts are u16, checked against the entire buffer, and do not need to fit the declared record. A 14-byte EXTTEXTOUT record can claim 65,535 text bytes beyond its own end. Ten thousand such records with enough trailing bytes imply 655,350,000 source bytes decoded into retained Strings from about 205.6 KB of WMF; UTF-8 conversion and later text handling can add cost.

dataflow.summary: DOCX image relationship → resolve_media → decode_image → metafile::render → raster_wmf text counts → wmf_text owned strings → retained texts vector.

likelihood.why: Malformed binary counts reach a built-in parser directly and bypass otherwise bounded stored input.

reachability.summary: The attacker controls embedded media in a document consumed by the renderer, with no release credentials or nondefault configuration.
reachability.outcome: Excessive allocation/work and host-process or WASM instance failure

attackPath.summary: Embed a placeable WMF with many underdeclared text records and inflated in-file text counts, and invoke DOCX rendering.

remediationTests: Deterministic parser tests with short declared records and text counts extending into the next record must refuse safely.
Cover EXTTEXTOUT options/rectangle, TEXTOUT padding and record-local geometry counts with small resource budgets.

findings.title: Scrubbing a document can preserve identifying properties at alternate part paths
findings.summary: Sharing the output of `scrub` can disclose author/company/custom properties when those metadata parts use nonconventional OPC relationship targets. The scrubber only visits fixed `docProps/core.xml`, `app.xml` and `custom.xml` paths and preserves other parts and relationships in its output.

severity.rationale: A recipient of a purportedly scrubbed document can read identifying metadata left inside the ZIP. The impact requires existing sensitive properties and an alternate metadata location, plus the owner relying on scrub before sharing; no public repository or network exposure is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: Evidence of routine producer files using alternate metadata paths and sensitive contents would increase likelihood; resolving metadata by relationship/content type or explicitly refusing unsupported layouts removes the gap.

confidence.rationale: Parent verified fixed-path edits, package relationship access, all-part output preservation and the sharing guarantee. No runtime round trip in Word or application reproduction was run.

codeEvidence.label: scrub guarantee
codeEvidence.code:
Removes who touched a document before it goes out: author names (as one
alias, `--author-alias NAME`), rsids, the people and dates in the document
properties, and comments. Text and tracked changes stay. Without a flag all
four go, under the alias "Author"; with flags, only those given.
codeEvidence.explanation: Users are told scrubbing removes identifying document properties before sharing.

codeEvidence.label: scrub input
codeEvidence.explanation: The public scrub operation reads the supplied package and selects the requested metadata removal.

codeEvidence.label: scrub call
codeEvidence.explanation: docprops invokes scrub_properties and returns the rewritten package when no new structural findings appear.

codeEvidence.label: scrub paths
codeEvidence.explanation: Core, extended and custom property parts are addressed by conventional fixed names.

codeEvidence.label: scrub core
codeEvidence.explanation: The implementation only edits/removes those fixed names; a relocated custom part does not even enter the relationship-removal branch.

codeEvidence.label: package relationships
codeEvidence.explanation: The package exposes its authoritative package-level relationships, but scrub_properties does not consult their targets.

codeEvidence.label: opc preserve
codeEvidence.explanation: Every surviving part is retained in the output entry list.

codeEvidence.label: opc write parts
codeEvidence.explanation: The output writer emits surviving part bytes and package relationships, so skipped metadata remains accessible to the recipient.

rootCause.summary: OPC metadata is identified by package relationships, but `scrub_properties` instead looks up three hard-coded names. Relocating a metadata part while retaining its relationship/content-type declaration causes the lookup to miss. The scrub output serializes all untouched parts and relationships, so structural validation does not remove or refuse the leftover identifying data.

findings.remediation: Resolve core, extended and custom property parts from package relationships and content types, sanitize every applicable internal target, and remove relationships/content-type entries together for custom properties. Refuse unsupported or ambiguous metadata layouts instead of returning a successfully scrubbed copy.

counterEvidence: Ordinary Word-generated conventional property paths are scrubbed.
Title, subject, body text and revision dates intentionally remain and are not claimed as leaks here.
Only newly introduced structural findings block output, so unchanged skipped metadata need not be free of preexisting findings.
limitations: Occurrence in ordinary producer files and actual sensitive values are unknown.
No live Word/open or runtime reproduction.
validation.summary: Verified the scrub call chain, all three fixed-path branches, and preservation of surviving parts/package relationships. Admission checks supported main document type and XML structure, not conventional metadata filenames; validation compares structural findings rather than enforcing anonymization. The finding is narrowed to docprops; author-alias traversal outside word/ was not independently validated as a separate issue.

dataflow.summary: Input property part at alternate relationship target → fixed-name lookup misses → unchanged package part/relationship → to_zip → shared outgoing DOCX.

impact.why: Potential identifying/confidential document properties exposed to an outgoing-document recipient.

likelihood.why: Requires alternate part layout, sensitive metadata and sharing after scrub.

reachability.summary: The recipient needs access to the shared scrubbed output, not the original source or victim machine. The owner must enable docprops, which the default scrub settings do.
reachability.outcome: Access to identifying property values intended to be removed

attackPath.summary: An owner scrubs and shares a package whose core/extended/custom properties use alternate internal targets; a recipient inspects the retained metadata part.

remediationTests: Integration tests relocate each metadata part and update its relationship/content type, then verify the same fields are removed from outgoing package bytes.
Cover multiple metadata relationships and conventional paths without losing unrelated intentional content.
